about: Swing screen of S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, and S&P MidCap 400 stocks. A name is published when the daily chart shows an oversold RSI, a lower Bollinger touch or re-entry, or a pullback while price is still above the 200-day average. RSI is Wilder's 14-day RSI. Bollinger Bands are the 20-day average plus and minus two population standard deviations. ATR is Wilder's 14-day average true range. The stop sketch is 1.5 times ATR under the last close. Targets are the 20-day average or the mid band, then the upper band, when those levels sit above the last close. The rank mixes that setup with fundamentals. Yahoo quoteSummary is tried first. If that crumb is blocked, Nasdaq's public quote, annual financials, analyst target, and earnings calendar are used instead: sector, industry, market cap, revenue growth, profit margin, free cash flow, debt-to-equity, forward P/E when Yahoo returns it, and the analyst target or consensus. Every sentence uses a fetched number. This is why a name screens as a swing candidate, not a guarantee and not financial advice. fetchedAt is when this file was last filled. A failed fetch keeps the previous rows.
disclaimer: Informational only, not financial advice and not a recommendation to buy or sell. A stock is listed because it matched a rules-based swing screen.
source: Yahoo Finance public daily chart API (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart). Fundamentals come from Yahoo quoteSummary (summaryProfile, summaryDetail, financialData, defaultKeyStatistics, calendarEvents) when the public crumb is available, otherwise from Nasdaq's public quote, financials, analyst target, ratings, and earnings calendar (https://api.nasdaq.com/).
